storyboard.claim: A guilt-driven yes is a mathematical disaster.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman professional frowning over a full to-do list, thinking through the cost of one extra yes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Picks up the guilt-driven yes from the parent's committee request.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the yes as arithmetic, not kindness.

storyboard.claim: Time is zero sum: every yes is a no to something else.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman professional talking, a full calendar behind her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the catastrophe into the rule behind it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the law: time cannot be created, only moved.

storyboard.claim: You cannot add hours; you must take them from something you already do.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman professional pondering, hands loosely held as if weighing where hours come from.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the zero-sum law with the practical consequence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says the extra hours are not free; they come out of something else.

storyboard.claim: The committee yes secretly means no to reading bedtime stories to your kids.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman professional thinking hard, a worried look, with no icon so the callout carries the bedtime cost.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Lists the first thing the yes quietly costs.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the hidden cost concrete: a parent's evening routine.

storyboard.claim: Saying yes to avoid discomfort sabotages your own life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman professional slumped, looking drained after a long day.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds sleep and the gym to the list of sacrificed things.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the trade-off its emotional price: your own life, to dodge a moment of awkwardness.

storyboard.claim: Corey Porier built a ruthless system to fight this trap.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Off-screen narrator voice; no person drawn.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the problem to the speaker who solved it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces Corey Porier by his method, not a portrait.

storyboard.claim: Every request for time is scored one to five by fit with core purpose.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Off-screen narrator voice; the scale is carried by the callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the system Porier uses.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the scoring mechanism: one to five, against a core purpose.

storyboard.claim: His core purpose is to donate, educate, inspire, motivate and entertain.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Off-screen narrator voice; the five purpose words sit on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Defines the purpose the scale measures against.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lists the purpose words so the viewer can judge what fits.

storyboard.claim: A request scoring under three is an automatic no, killed at the gate.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A door icon with the everyman professional pointing at it, turning requests away.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the scale into a rule of exclusion.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the no as a door that closes before the request enters.

storyboard.claim: Porier applies the same ledger to the people in his life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Off-screen narrator voice; the callout names the audit.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the purpose scale from requests to people.
storyboard.addedInformation: Signals the shift from calendar items to relationships.

storyboard.claim: He marks clients, associates and friends with a plus sign.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman professional holding a list of names with the notes in her hand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the ledger of people.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the list as a written ledger of names.

storyboard.claim: Plus marks go to people who radiate positive energy and add value.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman professional smiling warmly as she talks about the people who lift her up.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Defines the plus side of the ledger.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the plus its meaning: people who add value.

storyboard.claim: Minus marks go to people who complain and drain focus.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman professional slumped and worried, looking spent.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Defines the minus side of the ledger.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the cost of the minus side as lost focus.

storyboard.claim: He rebuilds his calendar to see more pluses and fewer minuses.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clock icon for the calendar schedule, with the everyman professional planning.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the ledger into schedule changes.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the calendar literal: schedule time is what gets rearranged.

storyboard.claim: The host objects: scoring human beings on a ledger sounds cold.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Off-screen narrator voice raising the objection.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The hosts push back on the ledger.
storyboard.addedInformation: Voices the skeptic's view the next beats will answer.

storyboard.claim: A good friend in divorce, job loss and depression will be negative.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman professional slumped with a sad face, the picture of a friend in crisis.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the skeptic's example: a friend who is struggling.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the case the ledger must not punish.

storyboard.claim: Putting a minus on a suffering friend and cutting them out would be wrong.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman professional worried, thinking about the harm of cutting someone out.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Carries the example to its harmful conclusion.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strikes the cold action the narrator rejects.

storyboard.claim: The hosts fear the ledger makes them a selfish friend and breeds narcissism.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman professional slumped in self-doubt.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Voices the fear from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the worry a self-image: the person who abandons friends.

storyboard.claim: A crisis of friendship is different from chronic behavioral patterns.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Off-screen narrator voice; the callout separates the two cases.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the selfish-friend worry.
storyboard.addedInformation: Distinguishes a temporary crisis from a standing pattern.

storyboard.claim: The audit is not about abandoning a loved one in tragedy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Off-screen narrator voice; the struck callout rejects abandonment.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Clarifies the scope of the audit.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says who the audit does not target: people in real crisis.

storyboard.claim: Some people are chronic emotional vampires who drain your energy by default.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman professional slumped and drained, as if her energy had been pulled out.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the group the audit targets.
storyboard.addedInformation: Defines the target: people whose complaining is their default.

storyboard.claim: These people dominate conversations, stir office drama and refuse help.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Off-screen narrator voice; the callout lists the behavior.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the vampires' behavior.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lists the recognizable traits of a chronic drain.

storyboard.claim: Protecting time and energy from these people is a vital defense, not narcissism.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shield icon, with the everyman professional explaining the defense.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the narcissism charge.
storyboard.addedInformation: Reframes the audit as protection of finite resources.

storyboard.claim: Like the airplane oxygen mask, secure your own energy before helping others.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman professional pointing at herself, the oxygen-mask rule in gesture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the airplane-mask principle.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the principle a physical gesture: yourself first.

storyboard.claim: If vampires drain you, nothing is left for family, friends or key tasks.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman professional slumped, empty and worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States the consequence of letting drains continue.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the emptiness that results from being drained.

storyboard.claim: Protecting your calendar is preservation of your capacity for those who matter.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Off-screen narrator voice; the struck callout rejects the cruelty charge.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Concludes the vampire argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the audit as care for the people who matter most.

storyboard.claim: Who gets your energy is a decision problem, not a scheduling problem.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A door icon for who gets access to your vault.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the vampire point into the book's decision frame.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says access to your energy is a choice you make at the door.

storyboard.claim: Sometimes the thing draining your time is a task you talked yourself into calling important.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman professional thinking, a self-deceiving look kept neutral.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from people draining you to tasks draining you.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the self-deception as the source of the drain.

storyboard.claim: The admin principle: the trap of fake work.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Off-screen narrator voice; the callout names the trap.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the admin principle.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the trap the next beats illustrate.

storyboard.claim: A startup CEO at 2 p.m. on a Tuesday is the example.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman professional standing as the stand-in for a founder, with the time on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Starts the startup founder example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets the time and role of the example.

storyboard.claim: The CEO should be the visionary steering toward an IPO.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A target icon for the strategic goal the CEO should aim at.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the job the CEO is meant to do.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets the strategic goal the CEO is supposed to be pursuing.

storyboard.claim: Instead, the CEO is comparing printer paper weights in a store aisle.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman professional thinking over a choice, standing as the shopper.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts the goal with the actual activity.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the misdirected task in a concrete everyday setting.

storyboard.claim: It is a tragedy of misallocated leverage that happens every day.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Off-screen narrator voice; the callout names the error.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the problem behind the printer-paper example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the error a label: leverage spent on the wrong work.

storyboard.claim: Harvard Business Review found 41% of knowledge workers' time goes to discretionary low-value work.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clock icon for time, with the 41 percent figure on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the example to the research.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the scale of the problem as a measured share of time.

storyboard.claim: The time goes to low-value activities others could handle.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman professional thinking about the tasks that could be handed off.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the 41 percent in more detail.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says the work could be delegated to someone else.

storyboard.claim: Strategy is ambiguous and its rewards are years away, so people avoid it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman professional thinking, weighing a distant reward.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why people choose the low-value task.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the reason strategy gets avoided: the payoff is far off.

storyboard.claim: Buying paper is simple and gives an immediate check off the list and a busy feeling.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman professional celebrating a quick win, a checked-off list.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts the quick win with the distant reward.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows why the low-value task feels rewarding in the moment.

storyboard.claim: Crossing items off the list is a complete illusion of progress.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman professional holding the notes list she has crossed items off.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Concludes the checkmark point.
storyboard.addedInformation: Calls the list-checking progress what it is: an illusion.

storyboard.claim: Kruse highlights a brutal quote from a venture capitalist.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Off-screen narrator voice introducing the quote.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the venture capitalist's line.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the quote about admin work.

storyboard.claim: A founder without an admin is doing admin work.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Off-screen narrator voice; the callout carries the quote.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Delivers the quote itself.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says the first hire should free the founder from admin work.
